title: Personal computer
summary: In 1977 three ready-built computers took personal computing beyond hobbyists. The Commodore PET came fully assembled with keyboard and cassette drive; Tandy Radio Shack's TRS-80, at $599.95 with screen and built-in BASIC, sold 10,000 units in its first month against a forecast of 3,000 a year; and Steve Wozniak's Apple II, sold complete with keyboard and case, offered colour graphics. All three became popular in schools and homes. Millions of Apple IIs sold by 1993, giving a generation its first access to computers.

uncertainty.note: Dated from the ready-built machines of 1977; personal computing continues.
